idiom_name: type object as [[Prototype]]: Object.create(type) and shared data properties
implementation_notes: JavaScript already guarantees the pattern's core: every object has a [[Prototype]] link to another object, property lookup walks that chain, and any object can play the role of a type - so Object.create(trollType) makes trollType the new object's type and the delegation the paper describes happens without a line of code. Class syntax is only sugar over the same [[Prototype]] chain, so there is exactly one realization here, not two: choose prototypes for data-loaded types and classes when you need instanceof identity or a constructor per type. The classic two-class structure remains justified when type identity must be visible to the type system (instanceof checks, serialisation with class names) or when per-type methods must be real functions. Type data parsed from JSON is frozen and registered in a Map; instance state lives as own properties shadowing the type's defaults.
pitfalls: Instances inherit the type's properties: assigning monster.health = 0 creates an own property that shadows the type's value, so later edits to type.baseHealth affect only newly spawned objects and leave the population inconsistent.

Type descriptors are mutable unless frozen - one stray assignment to types.get('troll').baseHealth retunes every instance that has not shadowed the property; Object.freeze (or deepFreeze) the catalogue on load.
Object.setPrototypeOf de-optimises an object's hidden class and hides the bug class above; set the type at construction with Object.create instead of switching types later.
